track: C (association -> track history -> temporal state -> re-acquisition)
registered: see the git commit that added this file (2026-10-05): before any corpus-v2 detection cache exists, before C1's VAL pass and before any forecaster-driven tracker has been run on VAL
class: controlled experiment on corpus-v2 VAL detection caches; tracker hyper-parameters cross-fitted over two VAL halves (by recording group) exactly as experiments/systems/scripts/track_eval.py; TEST untouched (a final system pass is registered separately)
question: Given a causal detector's per-frame detections, does temporal state estimation beat per-frame argmax, and does a better motion model -- the domain's TRAIN-best classical forecaster or the learned C1 forecaster -- beat the constant-velocity Kalman inside the same tracker?
prior_evidence: corpus-v1 VAL, symmetric-window detector (experiments/systems/reports/track_gen_temporal_fp_g4_full_e20_data_unified.md): STE (constant-velocity Kalman) vs argmax mSA +0.11 Anti-UAV IR, -0.33 Anti-UAV RGB, +1.85 CST (v1 holdout, incomplete corpus)
TRAIN (C1 tuning): the constant-velocity model is the wrong prior on gimbal footage (constant position 38.8 px vs constant velocity 74.0 px ADE, Anti-UAV IR); CST favours damped mean velocity

inputs.protocols: SOT (official start-frame box, then box or 'absent' per frame; Track A's mSA code on the official annotations) and MOT (no init box) for identity / continuity metrics

trackers.argmax@cf: per-frame best drone detection above a cross-fitted threshold (GRID_ARGMAX of track_eval.py)
trackers.ste_cv@cf: experiments/systems/scripts/ste.py unchanged (constant-velocity Kalman, size-scaled noise), GRID_STE of track_eval.py (504)
trackers.fste_classical@cf: forecaster-driven STE (experiments/aerotrack_temporal/scripts/tc_ste.py): the Kalman is replaced by the domain's TRAIN-best classical forecaster from runs/aerotrack_temporal/c1/classical_tuning.json (Anti-UAV: oudcv expected, CST: dcv expected -- whatever the file says) with a per-domain, per-horizon, per-axis variance = mean squared TRAIN residual of that forecaster on oracle histories
trackers.fste_learned@cf: the same tracker with the C1 model (learned, abs inputs, seed 0 checkpoint, its own predicted variance) -- run ONLY in domains where C1 adopts the learned forecaster (H1 SUPPORTED and H2 not LOSES); elsewhere marked NOT RUN (adoption rule)
trackers.fste_mechanics: per frame: k = frames since the last associated detection; prediction = the forecast made at that detection for horizon k (beyond 24: horizon-24 mean, variance x k/24); gate on d2 = sum over axes (c_det - mu_k)^2 / (var_k + (r_meas * max(size, 10))^2), r_meas = 1/20; best gated drone detection >= det_thr is associated and output (output = detection box); else a detection >= reacq_thr anywhere re-acquires (history restarts there); else coast (predicted box if coast_output) and after max_coast misses the target is declared absent; no track: best detection >= init_thr starts one. The learned forecaster is called when the last two frames are associated detections (its training condition); otherwise the domain's classical forecaster is used
trackers.fste_grid: det_thr {0.05, 0.15, 0.3} x init_thr {0.3, 0.5} x reacq_thr {0.5, 0.7, 0.9} x max_coast {0, 5, 20, 60} x coast_output {True, False} x gate_chi2 {9.21, 25.0}, max_coast 0 without coast_output dropped = 252 settings (the STE grid without its Kalman-only 'output' axis)

secondary: recovery time after re-entry and after loss (median / p90 / never; tc_track_metrics)
HOTA / DetA / AssA (TrackEval-identical), IDF1, MOTA, MT / ML, fragmentation, longest run (MOT protocol)
metrics.inference: paired per-sequence differences of cross-fitted SA (x 100), sequence bootstrap 95 % CI (B = 2000, seed 0), per group

H1_temporal_state.SUPPORTED: mean delta > +0.5 mSA and CI lower bound > 0

H2_domain_motion_model.SUPPORTED: mean delta > +0.5 mSA and CI lower bound > 0

H3_learned_motion_model.SUPPORTED: mean delta > +0.5 mSA and CI lower bound > 0

hypotheses.decided_per_group_and_detector: each hypothesis is decided per group on the primary cache; the secondary cache is a replication reported alongside (agreement / disagreement stated, no pooling)

adoption_rule: the deployed tracker per domain = the simplest tracker not beaten: start from argmax; move to ste_cv only if H1 SUPPORTED; to fste_classical only if H2 SUPPORTED (or if H1 is not SUPPORTED but fste_classical beats argmax by the same rule); to fste_learned only if H3 SUPPORTED. Ties keep the simpler tracker.

component_gate.measured_failure: on v1 the constant-velocity STE added ~0 mSA on Anti-UAV over argmax; its motion prior contradicts gimbal footage (TRAIN), so gating / coasting extrapolate in the wrong direction after a miss
component_gate.why: image-plane motion is mean-reverting (gimbal) or slow and inertial (CST): the predicted position used for gating and coasting should follow the domain's dynamics
component_gate.baseline: argmax@cf and ste_cv@cf with their own cross-fitted grids
component_gate.novelty: a tracker whose motion model is a calibrated forecaster chosen by an explicit, registered adoption rule, evaluated on identity / recovery metrics as well as SOT accuracy
component_gate.cost: classical: microseconds per frame; learned: one forecaster call per associated detection (ONNX Runtime CPU, < 1 ms)
component_gate.isolating_ablation: same tracker mechanics, only the motion model changes (H2, H3); temporal state vs none (H1)
component_gate.rtx5050: CPU-side; the detector stays on the GPU
component_gate.exportable: the tracker is Python / numpy; the learned forecaster exports to ONNX (checked: MLP parity 3.8e-6; the transformer is checked before use)
component_gate.falsifier: H2 and H3 NO_DIFFERENCE or HARMFUL on every group: the motion model does not matter for tracking with this detector, and the simplest adequate tracker is deployed

run_order: after C1's VAL pass (its adoption decision) and after tools/chains/post_v2_causal_caches.json produced the caches
experiments/aerotrack_temporal/scripts/tc_c3.py (CPU, at most 4 worker processes, never alongside another heavy CPU job while a GPU training runs)

amendments.when: 2026-10-05, before any C1c training and before this experiment's first run
amendments.what: the learned forecaster per domain is the one offered by the C1 / C1c adoption rule (preregistration/C1c_domain_aware_forecasting.json): the C1c model where C1c offers it, else C1's pooled model where C1 adopted it, else none
amendments.why: C1's pooled model loses on CST; C1c (registered before its training) tests camera-mode-aware models; downstream experiments must use whichever the registered rules adopt, decided without seeing their own results
